ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher, reverse the fee against the driver's record, and send the driver's cancellation/waiting-button use for account review (abuse of the "I'm Here" button).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the three chat messages [F8][F9][F10], the driver's statement [F12] and the complaint contain no threats, harassment, sexual remarks, abuse or dangerous-driving allegations — nothing to escalate on SAFE-1/SAFE-2. Safety screening is otherwise clear.

The dispute is a driver-cancelled no-show, so it enters via NS-0 (cancelled_by = driver, driver asserts rider no-show) and is tested against NS-1, with NS-2 as the fallback.

NS-1(i): the "I'm Here" tap itself is on record at 12:06:15 [F5], so the arrival indication exists.
NS-1(ii) FAILS: at the moment of the tap the driver was 600 m from the pickup point [F5], and his closest approach all trip was 599 m at 12:06:55 [F1] — never within the 200 m arrival radius, and the platform never recorded him at the pickup (driver_arrived_at null [F4]). [F2] confirms he was stationary 600 m away. The rider's contemporaneous "no car here" [F9] matches the GPS, and system records (gps/timeline) override the driver's post-hoc claim of having waited at the pickup [F12].
NS-1(iii) also fails: within-200 m time after the tap was 0 s [F5]; the ~3 min 30 s stationary period [F2] was spent 600 m away, which does not count as waiting at the pickup.

Because a required element of NS-1 is not met, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee [F3][F6] is refunded in full. The further NS-2 trigger also applies — the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 600 m from the pickup point [F5], Ryde's listed abuse of the cancellation/waiting button — so the account is flagged. NS-1's own safeguard (a GPS hole during waiting would send the case to a human) is not engaged: the trajectory is continuous and timestamped [F1][F2][F5].

Supporting context that does not change the outcome: no traffic incident on the route [F14] and only a mid-range speed band 3 on Jalan Besar [F13], so nothing supports a "reasonable cause" detour/position issue; weather fair [F15]. The rider's profile [F16] is clean; the driver's single prior upheld no-show [F17] is used only as context and is not the basis of this ruling. Evidence status is sufficient — the gps and timeline records settle every element needed (tap location, distance at tap, continuous coverage through cancellation, no platform arrival record).

Amount: $6.61 (the cancellation fee charged, per NS-2 full refund of that single disputed item, plus the NS-2 account flag). Confidence is 0.95 because the GPS/timeline evidence is unambiguous; the only residual uncertainty is semantic (the driver's untruthful statement), which the system-record rule resolves.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup and that the rider never showed up is contradicted by the system records: he tapped 'I'm Here' 600 m from the pickup [F5], was stationary 600 m away [F2], and never came within 200 m [F1]; no platform arrival was recorded [F4]. Under the procedure that gps/timeline records override statements, this claim is rejected.

Driver's chat 'I'm here already, please come out' at 12:06 asserts presence at the pickup, but GPS at that moment places him 600 m away [F5] and his closest approach was 599 m [F1]. Rejected as a claim of arrival.
